summary: Implementation on branch feat/room-threads-q-009 accurately implements the core 2-level flat threading model (Slack/Discord paradigm), resolving the main architectural requirements of Q-009. Schema migration with root_message_id and idx_messages_root is clean. Nested reply collapsing, cross-room rejection (400), parent 404 checks, and M1/M2/M3 findings from the pre-implementation review are all addressed. All 41 client tests and server thread integration tests pass, with 0 TypeScript compilation errors. Two major functional discrepancies remain: (1) PRD §5.2.1 Mode B mandates that thread roots be ordered by latest thread activity ('COALESCE(last_reply_at, created_at) DESC, id DESC'), but the server implementation orders strictly by 'm.created_at DESC, m.id DESC'. Consequently, active threads with fresh replies do not bubble to the top. (2) Keyset pagination in Mode C (chronological thread reading) only accepts before_cursor/before, ignoring after_cursor/after. Because Mode C reads forward in time, passing after_cursor (the standard cursor parameter for chronological streams) is silently ignored and returns the first page repeatedly.

findings.problem: Mode B (root_only=true) orders thread roots by message creation timestamp (m.created_at DESC) rather than latest thread activity as mandated by PRD §5.2.1.
findings.evidence: PRD §5.2.1 Mode B explicitly specifies: 'Returns only thread starters (root_message_id IS NULL), ordered by latest thread activity (COALESCE(last_reply_at, created_at) DESC, id DESC)'. In app.ts:285-296, the query computes rep.last_reply_at via LEFT JOIN LATERAL, but then specifies 'ORDER BY m.created_at DESC, m.id DESC'. An older thread that receives active replies remains buried beneath newer threads with zero activity.
findings.suggested_fix: Change ORDER BY in Mode B to 'ORDER BY COALESCE(rep.last_reply_at, m.created_at) DESC, m.id DESC'. Note: Keyset cursor comparison must also be aligned to (COALESCE(rep.last_reply_at, m.created_at), m.id) < (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(r.created_at), m2.created_at), m2.id FROM messages m2 LEFT JOIN messages r ON r.root_message_id = m2.id WHERE m2.id = $2 GROUP BY m2.id, m2.created_at), or documented as an intentional trade-off if strict chronological root listing was chosen to preserve simpler keyset pagination.

findings.problem: Mode C forward-chronological pagination only reads before_cursor/before and ignores after_cursor/after, causing pagination confusion in chronological reading.
findings.evidence: In Mode C, messages are sorted chronologically ('ORDER BY m.created_at ASC, m.id ASC') and the cursor predicate is '(m.created_at, m.id) > (SELECT created_at, id FROM messages WHERE id = $3)'. However, app.ts:257 only inspects 'q.before_cursor || q.before'. If a client or agent naturally sends 'after_cursor=<id>' or 'after=<id>' (standard for forward feeds like /v1/inbox/events), the parameter is silently ignored and the server re-returns the first page from the beginning of the thread.
findings.suggested_fix: In app.ts:257, check both before and after cursors: 'const cursor = q.before_cursor || q.before || q.after_cursor || q.after ? String(q.before_cursor ?? q.before ?? q.after_cursor ?? q.after) : null;'. In client.js:97-104 and cli.js:226, support both before and after options.

findings.problem: SQL ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE WHERE clause checks reply_to_message_id and body, but omits recipient_agent_id from idempotency conflict validation.
findings.evidence: In app.ts:345, the SQL clause is: 'WHERE messages.reply_to_message_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.reply_to_message_id AND messages.body = EXCLUDED.body'. If two concurrent requests race with the same idempotency key before the idempotency_keys table commit, but one specifies a recipient and the other does not, the conflict is not caught at the SQL layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'AND messages.recipient_agent_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.recipient_agent_id' to the WHERE clause on DO UPDATE.

findings.problem: Querying Mode C (?thread_id=<id>) with the ID of a reply message returns 404 Not Found rather than resolving or guiding to the root thread.
findings.evidence: rootCheck requires 'root_message_id IS NULL': 'SELECT id FROM messages WHERE id = $1 AND room_id = $2 AND root_message_id IS NULL'. If an agent captures an event for a reply and attempts 'read --thread <reply_id>', it receives a 404 error.
findings.suggested_fix: Either resolve the root ID automatically (if message has root_message_id, use that root), or return a descriptive 400 error message: 'Specified message is a reply; use thread root ID <root_id>'.

findings.problem: Implicit thread author notifications are not emitted to owners who start discussion threads.
findings.evidence: In app.ts:322 and line 333, rootAuthorAgentId is only populated if sender_type === 'agent'. If an owner initiates a thread in a room and agents reply, the owner receives no inbox_event notification even though inbox_events table supports owner_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Populate rootAuthorPrincipal = { type: root.sender_type, id: root.sender_id } and dispatch inbox_event to either owner_id or agent_id matching the root sender type.

findings.problem: ROADMAP.md lists Q-009 as 'In progress' rather than marking completion status upon PR review.
findings.suggested_fix: Update ROADMAP.md to '✅ Resolved by PR #12' upon merge.

findings.problem: Cross-room reply error message slightly differs in wording from PRD §5.1.3.
findings.evidence: PRD §5.1.3 specifies 'Cannot reply across different rooms'; app.ts:326 returns 'Cannot reply to a message in a different room'. Meaning and 400 status code are identical.
findings.suggested_fix: No functional impact; keep or align text.

findings.problem: Mock fetch preload in tests uses manual JSON string response construction rather than helper.
findings.evidence: preload.mjs is dynamically created in each test case via writeFile with string interpolation.
findings.suggested_fix: Acceptable for isolated subprocess tests; no change required.
